verdict.rationale: Parse returns layout-aware markdown, text, or JSON built for LLM pipelines, and tables can carry source-page provenance, so output is structured rather than raw text. RAG-ready segmentation comes only through the separate Index product (hosted vector search pipeline, selectable embedding models, vector-DB sinks), and those embedding and sink docs sit under deprecated paths; the Split API divides concatenated PDFs into documents, not RAG chunks. Missing for 10: documented chunking with semantic boundaries in Parse output, per-chunk metadata such as page numbers or section headers, embedding-ready segments without the deprecated Index pipeline, and independent hands-on corroboration of chunk quality.
